title: Linear and circular economies for plastics
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z write: failed the content check, writing again

draft.title: Linear and circular economies
card: plastic is made, used and then thrown away. The material is lost to landfill or the environment after one use.
plastic is kept in use for as long as possible. It is reused, recycled or broken down and made into new products.
Some condensation polymers, such as polyesters, can break down by hydrolysis. Water splits the links between monomers, which can return the monomers so they can be used again.
Better design also helps. A product made from one type of plastic is easier to sort and recycle than one made from a mix.
draft.remember: A linear economy ends in waste. A circular economy keeps the material in use.

a.q: Which choice describes a linear economy for plastics?
opts: Make a bottle, use it once, then send it to landfill
Make a bottle, use it, then recycle it into a new bottle
Make a bottle, use it, then break it into monomers
Make a bottle from one plastic so it is easy to sort
a.why: A linear economy goes from make to use to throw away. The recycling option is tempting but wrong, because it returns the material to use, which is circular.
a.clue: Look for the path that ends with the material being thrown away.

b.q: A company in Geelong makes a polyester that water can split back into its monomers. How does this help move towards a circular economy?
opts: The monomers can be recovered and made into new plastic
The plastic will last longer, so it never needs replacing
The plastic becomes an addition polymer that sorts easily
The monomers are lost, so less plastic reaches landfill
b.why: Hydrolysis splits the links of a condensation polymer, so the monomers can be collected and used again. Losing the monomers would not keep the material in use, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what happens to the monomers after water splits the chains.

a.best: Make a bottle, use it once, then send it to landfill

b.best: The monomers can be recovered and made into new plastic
